title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: MISSED BY THIS MORNING'S OWN NULL SWEEP — Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 TODAY, dated September 1 2026 on the platform release notes; `Fable 5.1` returned ZERO corpus matches and the 06:03 report explicitly recorded 'no frontier flagship dated Aug 31 or Sep 1'
bullets.summary: Read from the primary release notes, not from coverage. The September 1, 2026 entry launches Claude Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1`), successor to Fable 5 for long-running agentic coding, knowledge work and research, alongside Claude Mythos 5.1 (`claude-mythos-5-1`) for Project Glasswing participants only. Both carry a 1M token context window by default, 128k max output, always-on adaptive thinking, and Fable 5's own $10/$50 per MTok pricing - with one price cut: cache reads drop to $0.25/MTok, 0.025x base input against 0.1x on every other Claude model. Available on the Claude API to all customers plus Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry. Three changes are BREAKING for anything calling Fable 5: forced tool use (`tool_choice` of `any` or `tool`) now returns a 400; thinking blocks are bound to the producing model and no earlier model can read them; and editing anything before a thinking block - the system prompt, the tools array, or an earlier message - invalidates every later block, enforced for accounts created on or after August 31, 2026. Two behavior regressions matter for agent loops: parallel tool calling is more variable (one call per turn where Fable 5 batched several) and the model writes fewer progress updates during long tool runs. Noted as a source conflict: secondary aggregators date this release to August 2026 and one states that as of August 27 it was absent from the model catalog and release notes; the vendor's own release notes date it September 1, and per this report's standing rule the primary wins.
bullets.how: YES, and it is the day's most important item on both counts - what it is, and how it was found. The cache-read cut is the real economics: The Construct's fleet is exactly the workload it targets, long agentic sessions that re-read a cached prefix, and those sessions now pay a quarter of the Fable 5 cache-read rate. Against a pricing thread that has spent two days establishing that nothing else moved today, this is the only actual cost change on the board, and it moves the right way. The breaking changes are the operational work: any Construct agent that builds its own `messages` array - rather than running through Claude Code, the Agent SDK, or Managed Agents, all of which keep the prefix intact - must go append-only before migrating, moving per-turn reminders into turn-scoped system messages and tool changes into mid-conversation tool changes rather than rebuilding `system` or `tools`. The parallel-tool-call regression is the one that will show up as a silent bill increase rather than an error: more turns, more round trips, same answers, and the documented fix is a one-line batching instruction in the prompt. Stated as a limit - this report has not evaluated Fable 5.1 against any Construct workload, and the vendor's own guidance is to start with Opus 5 and reach for Fable 5.1 only for demanding long-horizon work, so this is a migration to scope, not one to run today.

bullets.title: BOTH HALVES of yesterday's cost thesis are dead, verified against Anthropic's own pricing page this morning: the September 1 Sonnet 5 increase to $3/$15 WILL NOT OCCUR, and the tokenizer claim beside it was wrong in figure, in scope, and in whether it was an event at all
bullets.summary: Two corrections from one primary source, platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, fetched directly rather than read through trade coverage. First: the model table lists Claude Sonnet 5 at $2/MTok input and $10/MTok output, with an explicit note that the $2/$10 pricing 'announced at launch as introductory pricing through August 31, 2026, is now the standard price' and that the September 1 increase 'will not occur.' Secondary coverage dates the reversal to an August 10 announcement, attributing it to competitive pressure with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol at comparable rates. Today is September 1 and the rate is unchanged - yet this corpus carried the increase on 08-25 and again as the lead bullet of 08-31, where it was stated as taking effect 'tomorrow', and `will not occur` returned ZERO matches across every file in this directory. Second: yesterday's bullet 5 reported from an aggregator that the repricing 'ships with a tokenizer change that adds roughly 10-35% more tokens on code.' The primary says approximately 30% more tokens for the same text, scoped to Claude 4.7-and-later MODELS rather than to code, with Sonnet 4.6 and earlier on the previous tokenizer. Today's Fable 5.1 documentation independently restates the same figure and the same scope. It is a standing property of a model generation, not a September 1 event.
bullets.how: YES, and the applicability is to this report before it is to the business. Operationally the easy half: the Sonnet 5 run rate does not move today, $2/$10 is permanent rather than promotional, and the budget line yesterday's report told Bobby to expect to rise by 50% stays flat. The tokenizer correction matters more because it changes what the number means rather than merely whether it applies - yesterday's arithmetic multiplied a 1.5x rate rise by a 1.1-1.35x token rise to reach '1.65-2.0x' on coding-heavy agents, and with the rate rise cancelled and the tokenizer effect revealed as pre-existing, the correct statement is that per-token cost is unchanged today AND token counts are unchanged today. The ~30% premium is already baked into every invoice the fleet has generated since it moved onto 4.7-class models; it was never a delta. What survives is a genuine planning constant, vendor-sourced and now doubly confirmed: ~30% more tokens for the same text on 4.7-and-later, useful for comparing a Sonnet 4.6 quote against a Sonnet 5 quote or sizing a context budget from an older estimate. Stated as a limit - the doc says the exact increase depends on content and workload shape, and this has still not been measured against a real Construct workload.

bullets.title: The one dated cost event that survives verification: the September 14 Claude Code weekly-limit reset is real and unretracted, and a scope detail newly carried today is that it hits paid seat-based plans ONLY, not API-key or usage-based Enterprise
bullets.summary: Re-checked deliberately rather than assumed, precisely because the items beside it turned out to be stale. It holds. The ClaudeDevs post of August 29 stands unretracted: starting September 14, standard weekly Claude Code limits rise permanently by 25% for Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans, with the current temporary 50% increase in place until then. The arithmetic is unchanged - a pre-promotion baseline of 100 became 150 under the boost and resets to 125, which is 16.7% below today's cap and rounds to the 17% figure Anthropic itself states. The scope detail this corpus had not previously recorded: the change applies to paid seat-based plans only; free, usage-based Enterprise, and API-key customers are explicitly not included. Corroborated independently today by trade coverage confirming the +50% promotional window ended August 31.
bullets.how: YES, and with today's pricing corrections it is now the only dated capacity or cost event left on the calendar, thirteen days out. The scope detail is the operational hook and it reframes the question: The Construct's agents split across seat-based Claude Code usage and API-key usage, only the former is affected, so the real question is not 'how much capacity do we lose' but 'which of Hermes, Lens, Mallard, Pulse and the PRAGMA operators run against the seat limit rather than an API key.' One `/cost` and `/usage` reading answers that directly and no further reading will. Stated plainly: the fleet only feels a cut if it is currently saturating the boosted cap on seat-based plans; a fleet running under the cap experiences a 25% increase instead. This report has now carried that measurement unpulled for eight days, and the recommendation stands - take the reading this week or drop the item rather than carry it a ninth time.

bullets.title: A COST DIMENSION THIS CORPUS HAS NEVER CARRIED: Claude Managed Agents bills SESSION RUNTIME at $0.08 per session-hour separately from tokens - `session-hour` returns ZERO matches despite `Managed Agents` appearing in six prior files
bullets.summary: Read directly from the pricing page. Claude Managed Agents bills on two dimensions, not one: all tokens at standard model rates, plus a session-runtime SKU at $0.08 per session-hour, metered to the millisecond and accruing only while a session's status is 'running' - time spent idle waiting for a message or a tool confirmation, rescheduling, or terminated does not count. Session runtime replaces the code-execution container-hour billing model on that path, so it is a substitution rather than an addition. Anthropic's worked example: a one-hour Opus 5 session consuming 50k input and 15k output tokens costs $0.25 + $0.375 + $0.08 runtime = $0.705. Two modifiers do not apply - the Batch API 50% discount (sessions are stateful and interactive) and partner cloud-platform pricing.
bullets.how: MAYBE. It earns a bullet because of the shape of The Construct's workload: this fleet runs LONG agents, and a runtime meter prices long agents differently from token-only billing in a way that stays invisible until the invoice arrives. The mitigating detail is what keeps it a maybe - runtime accrues only while 'running', and an agent that spends most of its wall-clock time idle between tool confirmations is billed for very little of it, which is exactly the shape of a Hermes deploy job or a Pulse scan waiting on searches. At $0.08/hour the absolute numbers are small; runtime is 11% of Anthropic's own worked example and would be a larger share of a smaller, token-light bill. The honest position: know this dimension exists before moving anything onto Managed Agents, not a reason to move or not move. Stated as a limit - this report does not know whether any Construct agent runs on Managed Agents at all, and the same unpulled `/cost` reading would settle that too.

bullets.title: NULL SWEEP, AMENDED - the Anthropic null recorded at 06:03 is now FALSIFIED by bullet 1, but the other four categories hold on a re-check at 14:00, and the signage / wayfinding / permitting MCP negative reaches an ELEVENTH consecutive day
bullets.summary: This morning's sweep recorded five nulls; the re-check at 14:00 breaks one and confirms four. BROKEN: 'no frontier flagship dated Aug 31 or Sep 1' was false when written - Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 are dated September 1 on the vendor's release notes, and the third-party trackers this sweep relies on had not picked them up, still returning Qwen3.8 Flash (Aug 26) as the most recent release. That is the mechanism of the miss and it is recorded as such. HOLDS: no release dated Aug 31 or Sep 1 from OpenAI, Google, Meta, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek or Cohere, with OpenAI's line still GPT-5.6 Sol/Luna/Terra from July; no MCP server released in the window, the newest surfaced items being the 2026-07-28 spec, the August 22 roadmap and Okta's weekly OSS update, all carried; no agent funding round dated Aug 31-Sep 1, the trackers returning Q3-to-date rounds already logged; and no arXiv agent-architecture or context-engineering paper outside the corpus. Two funding zero-matches logged WITHOUT a bullet precisely because their dates could not be verified and this report's own rule forbids presenting an undated aggregator line as news: Legora's $550M Series D at $5.55B and Assort Health's $120M Series C at $1.2B, both absent from every file here, both to be date-checked before they are ever carried. And an eleventh consecutive direct search for a signage, wayfinding or permitting MCP server returned only sign-company marketing and generic protocol-security material, with no trade tooling whatsoever.
bullets.how: NO on the market items, and the sweep is written down because a checked null differs from an assumed one - a distinction this scan has now been burned by from BOTH directions in a single day, first by restating a cancelled price as fact and then by recording a same-day model launch as absent. The signage negative at eleven days is the one worth restating: the trade Brand 9 actually operates in still has no agent-callable surface, nobody is building one, and eleven consecutive daily checks is long enough that this is a fact about the market rather than a gap in the searching. The corresponding observation stands unchanged - whoever builds the permitting or wayfinding-spec layer first has no incumbent to displace. This report is not recommending building it; it is recording that the window has stayed open for eleven days of looking.

praxis_lesson: Both of today's failures were the same failure wearing different clothes, and the second arrived four hours after the first was diagnosed. This morning the report corrected a cancelled price it had restated as fact, and drew the right rule: verify a dated change against the vendor's own page. Then, in the same file, it declared 'no frontier flagship dated Aug 31 or Sep 1' on the authority of third-party release trackers - and Anthropic had shipped Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 that day, on its own release-notes page, which the report never opened. The lesson is therefore narrower and more useful than this morning's version: a NEGATIVE about a specific vendor is a claim about that vendor's own channel, and it is worth exactly what the channel check behind it is worth. Trackers lag; release notes do not. The fix is one line in the sweep - open the primary release notes of any vendor the report is about to declare quiet, and reserve the aggregators for vendors it has no channel for. Stated as a discipline: this report may say 'the trackers show nothing', and it may say 'Anthropic shipped nothing', but it may only say the second after reading Anthropic's page.
